# Incident Report — MTA 2024-09-04 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Victim Host
| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | 172.17.0.99 |
| MAC address | 18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4 |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-RNVO9AT |
| AD domain | bepositive.com (realm BEPOSITIVE.COM, DC = 172.17.0.17 / WIN-CTL9XBQ9Y19.bepositive.com) |
| Logged-in Windows user | afletcher (confirmed via Kerberos AS-REQ CNameString, 172.17.0.99 → 172.17.0.17, 21:34:35 UTC+4) |

## Malware Family
**Koi Stealer** (Win32/Koi Stealer). **Signature-confirmed** — ETPRO rule "ETPRO TROJAN Win32/Koi Stealer CnC Checkin (POST) M2" fired 48 times directly on the POST /foots.php traffic from 172.17.0.99 to 79.124.78.197. This is corroborated behaviorally: fixed-IP C2 (no DNS lookup ever performed for it), spoofed legacy IE7 user-agent, small encrypted octet-stream POST bodies on a steady ~60-90 second beacon interval from 21:35 to 22:31 UTC+4.

## Indicators of Compromise

**C2 endpoint (confirmed, signature + behavioral)**
- `79.124.78.197:80` (HTTP, no TLS)
- Beacon: `POST /foots.php` — Content-Type: application/octet-stream, Content-Encoding: binary, bodies 40-112 bytes (encrypted/opaque), server replies `200 OK` empty body. ~55 check-ins over 57 minutes.
- User-Agent on every C2 request: `Mozilla/4.0 (compatible; MSIE 7.0; Windows NT 10.0; WOW64; Trident/7.0; .NET4.0C; .NET4.0E; .NET CLR 2.0.50727; .NET CLR 3.0.30729; .NET CLR 3.5.30729)`
- Registration/loader exchange on the same host, tcp.stream 51 (21:35:11):
  - `GET /index.php?id=&subid=qIOuKk7U` → response `HckDcK0czXjaq48jVHNn|qIOuKk7U|http://79.124.78.197/index.php|` (bot ID `HckDcK0czXjaq48jVHNn`, affiliate/subid `qIOuKk7U`)
  - `POST /index.php` (105-byte encrypted body) → response `D` (single-byte ack)
- No domain resolves to 79.124.78.197 anywhere in the capture; the malware calls the raw IP.

**Suspected delivery/dropper channel (behavioral, timing-correlated only)**
- `46.254.34.201:443`, TLS SNI `www.bellantonicioccolato.it` — TCP session opens at 21:35:04, 2.6 seconds before the first Koi Stealer C2 beacon (21:35:07). ~719 KB exchanged in a 102-second burst (~701 KB inbound to the victim), consistent in size/shape with a payload download immediately preceding first check-in. Traffic is TLS-encrypted, so no file name or hash is recoverable from the capture; flagging this as the likely delivery vector by timing/volume correlation, not as a confirmed dropper.

**No malicious file names or SHA256 hashes are recoverable from this capture.** All payload-sized transfer occurred over TLS (46.254.34.201) and all C2 POST/GET bodies to 79.124.78.197 were binary/encrypted — no cleartext executable was carried over plaintext HTTP in this pcap.

## Alerts reviewed and assessed as benign (not part of the compromise)
- ET INFO "Terse Request for .txt" / "Microsoft Connection Test" to 23.220.251.149 / 23.220.251.158 — legitimate Windows NCSI check (`www.msftconnecttest.com`).
- GPL NETBIOS SMB (NTLMSSP/session-setup "overflow"), GPL RPC Kerberos principal name "overflow" — all sport/dport pairs are 172.17.0.99 ↔ 172.17.0.17 (workstation ↔ its own AD DC). This is normal Kerberos/LDAP/SMB domain-logon and SAMR traffic (legacy GPL signatures over-fire on stock AD chatter); no SMB share/filename evidence of exploitation or lateral movement was found.
- `acroipm2.adobe.com` GET /assets/Owner/arm/ProcessMAU.txt (Adobe ARM update check) and all `*.microsoft.com`/`*.msn.com`/`ctldl.windowsupdate.com` traffic — standard Windows/Office/Adobe background activity, resolved to legitimate Akamai/Microsoft/Azure infrastructure.

## Bottom line
DESKTOP-RNVO9AT (172.17.0.99, MAC 18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4), logged in as domain user afletcher on bepositive.com, was infected with Koi Stealer. Likely delivered via a TLS session to www.bellantonicioccolato.it (46.254.34.201) immediately before infection. The malware beacons to 79.124.78.197:80 using /foots.php (checkin) and /index.php (registration, bot ID HckDcK0czXjaq48jVHNn / subid qIOuKk7U), spoofing an IE7 user-agent. All payload and C2 traffic bodies are encrypted, so no file names or hashes could be extracted from network evidence alone.
